# Matt Waldman's RSP Cast — 2024-02-01

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/rsp-cast/2024-02-01-rsp-2024-sr-bowl-fallout-and-fave-developmental-picks-going-deep-with-bran.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

*Going Deep* with co-host [[Brandon Angelo]] (tracked). A dense, prospect-only
episode built around Senior Bowl/Shrine Game week — no current-NFL content.
Per this wiki's durability guidance, Senior Bowl and developmental-prospect
evaluation is treated as high-value: these are 2024 draft prospects who are
3rd-year pros as of this ingest, so the calls and how they aged are directly
checkable.

**Opens with a personal aside from Angelo** worth noting on his own expert
page: he was a Big Ten sprinter and personally raced [[Tyreek Hill]] twice
(100m and 200m) at a U.S. junior national trials event when Hill was still
a high schooler committed to Oklahoma State — "there's levels to
athleticism... he wasn't just good, he was that good and better."

**What Senior Bowl week is actually for**, per both hosts: reading which way
NFL scouts' private opinions are trending (via reporters like Daniel
Jeremiah and Bucky Brooks), gauging the depth of a draft class's middle
tier (last year's example: [[Tank Dell]] and [[Puka Nacua]] both shined in
Mobile), watching small-school players test directly against Power Five
competition, and — Angelo's specific addition — reading which
recently-injured players look not just talented again but competitively
healthy. See [[Healthy Enough to Play vs. Healthy Enough to Perform]] and
[[Prospect Pro-Readiness vs Ceiling]], both directly extended this episode.

**Receivers.** [[Ricky Pearsall]] and [[Malachi Corley]] get reinforced as
players both hosts were already high on. New pages: [[Roman Wilson]]
(Michigan), [[Devontez Walker]] (UNC — a real stock disagreement between
outside buzz and Angelo's own grade), [[Brendan Rice]] (USC), [[Dylan Laube]]
(New Hampshire — a small-school riser both hosts want to revisit), and
[[J. Michael Sturdivant]] (UCLA). [[Xavier Legette]] gets tempered — real
in-person Senior Bowl reps read "sloppier" and less dominant than his frame
suggested.

**Quarterbacks.** [[Spencer Rattler]] gets a maturity/leadership storyline
alongside on-field notes. [[J.J. McCarthy]], [[Drake Maye]] and [[Bo Nix]]
all get substantially extended, more skeptical reads than their prior
January entries — Angelo independently downgrades Nix after watching him
throw live at the Senior Bowl ("Mitch Trubisky syndrome"), a real
disagreement with Waldman's more bullish 2024-01-22 take. [[Michael Penix Jr.]] gets an updated, more specific medical-contingent draft-range
call. New pages for three purely developmental arm-talent QBs: [[Tanner Mordecai]], [[Jack Plummer]] and [[Joe Milton III]] (the last an extended,
vivid breakdown — Malik Willis comp, "Jordan Love treatment" recommended).

**Running backs and a tight end.** New pages: [[Ray Davis]] (Kentucky),
[[Deshaun Fenwick]] (Oregon State, Shrine Game), and [[Mario Anderson]] (a
name Waldman flags as one to watch for a future class, not this one's
draft-eligible group). New page for [[Brevyn Spann-Ford]] (Minnesota TE),
the episode's most detailed single breakdown — a long, specific
before/after read on blocking technique and pass-pro improvement across
2022 into late 2023, ending on real optimism for a practice-squad/depth-TE
NFL outcome.

## Not given pages

Will Levis (used only as a grading-history comp for [[J.J. McCarthy]] — both
hosts admit they graded him as a non-prospect pre-draft; logged as a
track-record note on the expert pages rather than a standalone page, since
no forward-looking evaluative claim is made about him here), Devaughn Vele
and an unidentified second Utah name (mentioned in passing, no real
evaluation), a torn-ACL prospect referred to in the transcript as "Rashan
Rashin Ali" (too badly garbled by the ASR to confidently resolve to a real
name — per rule 7, omitted rather than guessed), LeGarrette Blount and
Brian Westbrook (historical Senior-Bowl anecdotes, not current-class
evaluation), Jimmy Graham and DeMarco Murray (comps/anecdotes only).
